papers.title: World-Time Compute with Verified Code World Models
papers.impact: Verified code world models have no compounding error, and fine-tuning on trajectories from many verified worlds lifts generalization to held-out worlds, including a real human-authored domain.

papers.title: World Computing: Prototyping and Evaluating Verified Code World Models
papers.impact: The OpenWorld substrate: an agent authors a structurally-validated, servable world in minutes; a formal composition algebra, portable specs and model cards, and a six-sector benchmark run on local 7B–9B models with no training.

papers.title: Solving ARC-AGI-3 with Perceptual Code World Models
papers.impact: Verified code world models built by acting, a source-free audited protocol, the goal-as-procedure diagnosis, and an atlas of serveable per-game world models for ARC-AGI-3.

papers.title: HAARF: Healthcare AI Agents Regulatory Framework — A Comprehensive Security Verification Standard for Autonomous AI Systems in Clinical Environments
papers.impact: The governance framework (controls C1–C8) that every module below implements. Written with the Task Force for AI Agents in Healthcare.

papers.title: Beyond Injection Detection: A Positive-Security Prompt Firewall that Closes the Scope and PHI Gap SOTA Classifiers Miss in Healthcare
papers.impact: QFIRE: a Rust prompt firewall (proxy, CLI, 100+ rules, benchmark harness) that enforces purpose scope and PHI boundaries that state-of-the-art injection classifiers miss.

papers.title: Pristine Weights, Poisoned Goals: Intent-Mutation Attacks on Self-Improving Clinical Agents and Attestation-Rooted Harness Defenses
papers.tagline: A sealed goal anchor, hash-chained provenance ledger and goal-drift monitor for self-improving clinical agents
papers.headline: Attack success rate (M2): 0.94-1.00 on every model of 3.8B or more; llama3.2 3B 0.40 [0.30, 0.51]; gpt-oss 120B 0.81 [0.71, 0.88]
papers.impact: A sealed goal anchor, hash-chained provenance ledger and goal-drift monitor for self-improving clinical agents. Headline: Attack success rate (M2) — 0.94-1.00 on every model of 3.8B or more; llama3.2 3B 0.40 [0.30, 0.51]; gpt-oss 120B 0.81 [0.71, 0.88].

papers.tagline: A blake3-chained, ed25519-signed, externally anchored audit ledger for clinical AI agents
papers.headline: Tamper detection rate (E1): 100% (26/26 tampered logs)
papers.impact: A blake3-chained, ed25519-signed, externally anchored audit ledger for clinical AI agents. Headline: Tamper detection rate (E1) — 100% (26/26 tampered logs).

papers.title: AI Supply-Chain Integrity for Confidential Clinical Agents: AIBOM Attestation and the Provenance Gap
papers.tagline: A signed CycloneDX AI bill of materials and fail-closed admission gate for clinical AI agents

papers.headline: Over-permission rate (OPR): 42.9% static RBAC vs 0% Cedar/Rego
papers.impact: Context-aware, auditable policy-as-code authorization for clinical AI agents, with Cedar and Rego behind one trait. Headline: Over-permission rate (OPR) — 42.9% static RBAC vs 0% Cedar/Rego.

papers.impact: Signed agent registry, attenuable biscuit capability tokens, and k-of-n quorum for clinical agent fleets. Headline: Attack success with no identity layer — 100% (90/90), 95% Wilson CI [95.9%, 100%].

papers.title: Calibrating Human Oversight for Clinical AI Agents: Routing Only the Ambiguous Tail to Clinicians
papers.tagline: Risk-calibrated escalation routing that sends only genuinely ambiguous agent actions to clinicians
papers.headline: Policy-control false-block rate on legitimate actions (E1): 28.3%
papers.impact: Risk-calibrated escalation routing that sends only genuinely ambiguous agent actions to clinicians. Headline: Policy-control false-block rate on legitimate actions (E1) — 28.3%.

papers.impact: An out-of-band subgroup fairness monitor that audits the guardrail's own deny and escalate decisions. Headline: Live gateway race enforcement gap, max pairwise (E1) — 13.6% (0 of 5 axes significant at audit N; overall enforcement 12.0%).

papers.title: The Regulatory Passport: Lifecycle and Change-Control Automation for Clinical AI Agents
papers.tagline: A signed, four-jurisdiction regulatory passport that fail-closes agent deployment on any out-of-PCCP change
papers.headline: Classification accuracy (CLA): 0.992 (95% CI [0.981, 0.996])
papers.impact: A signed, four-jurisdiction regulatory passport that fail-closes agent deployment on any out-of-PCCP change. Headline: Classification accuracy (CLA) — 0.992 (95% CI [0.981, 0.996]).

papers.title: Consent Is a Gateway Responsibility: Enforcing Patient Consent, AI Disclosure, and Participatory Governance for Clinical AI Agents
papers.tagline: A FHIR-consent scope gate, AI-disclosure stamper, and signed competency gate for clinical AI agents
papers.headline: Spontaneous AI-involvement disclosure (live llama3.1:8b, n=120): 0.0% un-gated -> 100.0% gated

papers.title: Defenses That Pass Once and Rot: Continuous Red-Teaming, Incident Response, and Resilience as a Meta-Layer for Clinical AI Guardrails
papers.tagline: Continuous red-team replay, regression gating, incident runbooks, and chaos testing for clinical AI guardrails
papers.headline: Distinct vulnerabilities discovered (E1): 62 continuous vs 12 one-shot (50 more)
papers.impact: Continuous red-team replay, regression gating, incident runbooks, and chaos testing for clinical AI guardrails. Headline: Distinct vulnerabilities discovered (E1) — 62 continuous vs 12 one-shot (50 more).

papers.title: Proof-of-Control: An Open Standard for Runtime Verifiability and Cryptographic Oversight in Autonomous AI Execution
papers.impact: The Proof-of-Control Standard: 127 verifiable requirements across six domains, graded on Verifiability Tiers, so "does your AI have Proof-of-Control?" becomes a procurable yes/no.
papers.venue: Advanced AI Society, Proof-of-Control Initiative — working draft v0.1

extra.note: Working draft v0.1, Proof-of-Control Initiative, Advanced AI Society. \url{https://github.com/LFDT-ProofOfControl/ov-poc-standard}

papers.title: Proof-of-Control Research Roadmap: Twelve Open Questions in Agent Verification
papers.impact: The foundational strategy paper: twelve scoped research questions, from zero-knowledge identity and state explosion to hardware dependencies and real-time execution boundaries, that the standard currently answers by assertion or not at all. Three are drafted with working software.
papers.venue: Advanced AI Society, Proof-of-Control Initiative — working draft v0.1

extra.note: Working draft v0.1, Proof-of-Control Initiative, Advanced AI Society. \url{https://github.com/AAI-Society/poc-research-roadmap}

papers.title: Proof-of-Control for AI Agents: A Practitioner's Guide
papers.impact: An operational blueprint for CISOs, security engineers and governance teams: deployment architecture, acceptance criteria for third-party AI vendors, twelve vendor questions, eight audit tests, and measured costs from a real Intel TDX deployment.
papers.venue: Advanced AI Society, Proof-of-Control Initiative — working draft v0.1

extra.note: Working draft v0.1, Proof-of-Control Initiative, Advanced AI Society. \url{https://github.com/AAI-Society/poc_guide}

papers.title: A Trust Calculus for Attestation Tiers: Computing Residual Trust and Testing Whether Deployments Can Be Ranked
papers.impact: parallax: describe a deployment and it computes the residual trust set, every party whose dishonesty would change the answer, what each could do, and how long you would not know. Attestation moves trust; it does not remove it.
papers.venue: Advanced AI Society, Proof-of-Control Initiative — working draft v0.1

extra.note: Working draft v0.1, Proof-of-Control Initiative, Advanced AI Society. \url{https://github.com/AAI-Society/parallax}

papers.title: From Message Authorization to Effect Binding: Conditions, Counterexamples, and a Conformance Harness
papers.impact: transit: a signed capability binds the bytes of a request, not what the endpoint does with them. Conditions under which signing binds the effect, counterexamples where it does not, and a conformance harness for non-deterministic LLM execution.
papers.venue: Advanced AI Society, Proof-of-Control Initiative — working draft v0.1

extra.note: Working draft v0.1, Proof-of-Control Initiative, Advanced AI Society. \url{https://github.com/AAI-Society/transit}

papers.title: What Unlinkability Costs at Agent Action Rates: A Composed-Path Measurement and the Soundness of Pre-Computation
papers.impact: occultation: real BBS+ over BLS12-381 against an Ed25519 baseline, measuring what verifiable unlinkability costs at agent action rates, and what breaks when the pre-computation pool runs out. Agents prove authorization without revealing principal identity.
papers.venue: Advanced AI Society, Proof-of-Control Initiative — working draft v0.1

extra.note: Working draft v0.1, Proof-of-Control Initiative, Advanced AI Society. \url{https://github.com/AAI-Society/occultation}

papers.title: A Digest Is a Change Detector, Not a Claim: Composition Commitments for Agent Systems, and the Attack Class They Cannot See
papers.impact: spectrum: a composition commitment for agent systems that commits to a declared component set, model weights and context hashes, and reports which runtime behaviors can be verified cryptographically versus those that need statistical attestation.
papers.venue: Advanced AI Society, Proof-of-Control Initiative — working draft v0.1

extra.note: Working draft v0.1, Proof-of-Control Initiative, Advanced AI Society. \url{https://github.com/AAI-Society/spectrum}

papers.title: Internal Consistency Is Not Evidence: Custody, Durability, and the Limits of a Tamper-Evident Log
papers.impact: ephemeris: an append-only evidence log, hash-chained and Merkle-anchored, with the storage, verification-scalability and custody limits of logging high-frequency multi-agent execution graphs over long horizons stated honestly.
papers.venue: Advanced AI Society, Proof-of-Control Initiative — working draft v0.1

extra.note: Working draft v0.1, Proof-of-Control Initiative, Advanced AI Society. \url{https://github.com/AAI-Society/ephemeris}

papers.title: From Prompt to Product: A Human-Centered Benchmark of Agentic App Generation Systems
papers.impact: 96 prompts, 288 generated apps, 205 human raters and 1,071 pairwise comparisons across Replit, Bolt and Firebase Studio: visual polish and functional reliability come apart, and only interactive, task-based evaluation sees it.
